baths_guide.text: Tablets cursing thieves were thrown into the spring: 'May he who stole my cloak lose his mind and his eyes.' Roman customer service.
Roman pipes were made of lead, so please do not drink the water. The Romans did anyway. Hmm.

baths_visitor.text: It's steaming! I thought the steam was a special effect. It's actually the spring. Brilliant.

then.text: Sulis thanks you. She said so in the steam. It sounded like a kettle, but I choose to hear it as thanks.
A stall in the town square, you say? Selling the overflow? In bottles?
Right. I've kept this spring for thirty years. I'm going to have a quiet word. It will be a very loud quiet word.
She sets off through the colonnade, her keys jangling like a small, furious wind chime.
Take this. It's what the Romans would have wanted. Or at least what the tea room would have wanted.

else.text: Sulis's spring has run for two thousand years. The Romans threw coins in it. The Georgians drank from it. And now somebody wants to bottle it and call it 'heritage'.
Someone's selling bottles out in the square. I can't leave the spring. If you could find out where they got the water, I'd be so grateful.
